definition: An early and influential family of models that learned word embeddings from large corpora using shallow neural networks.
details: Word2Vec introduced the continuous bag-of-words (CBOW) and skip-gram objectives, predicting a word from its context or vice versa. Its embeddings captured semantic and syntactic regularities — famously king − man + woman ≈ queen — and demonstrated that cheap, fast models could learn rich word meaning from raw text.

explainer.lead: Word2Vec is an early, influential family of models that learned word embeddings from large corpora using shallow neural networks. It mattered because cheap, fast models proved that rich word meaning could be learned from raw text.

tiers.eli5: It reads huge amounts of text and places words with similar meanings close together on a map, so 'king' ends up near 'queen'.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train skip-gram or CBOW objectives to get reusable vectors for downstream tasks; a pitfall is that embeddings reflect the text they were trained on, regularities and biases alike.
